niyyah.name: Intention
niyyah.posture: Stand upright, facing the Qibla, feet slightly apart, eyes toward the place of prostration.
niyyah.translation: Intend in your heart the prayer you are about to perform. The intention is silent — it is not pronounced aloud.
niyyah.note: The intention belongs to the heart. Saying it out loud is not part of the prayer.

takbir.name: Opening Takbir
takbir.posture: Raise both hands to the level of your shoulders or ears, then place your right hand over your left.
takbir.note: This Takbir opens the prayer. From here on, ordinary speech and movement are no longer allowed.

istiftah.name: Opening supplication
istiftah.posture: Standing, hands folded over the chest or the stomach.
istiftah.phonetic: Subhaanaka Allaahumma wa bihamdika, wa tabaaraka smuka, wa ta'aalaa jadduka, wa laa ilaaha ghayruk
istiftah.translation: Glory be to You, O Allah, and all praise is Yours. Blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god but You.
istiftah.note: A recommended act (sunnah), said once, quietly, at the start of the first unit only. Other wordings are also transmitted.

taawwudh.name: Seeking refuge
taawwudh.translation: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan, the rejected.
taawwudh.note: Said quietly before the first recitation of the Qur'an.

fatiha.name: Al-Fatiha
fatiha.phonetic:
Bismillaahi r-Rahmaani r-Raheem
Al-hamdu lillaahi Rabbi l-'aalameen
Ar-Rahmaani r-Raheem
Maaliki yawmi d-deen
Iyyaaka na'budu wa iyyaaka nasta'een
Ihdinaa s-siraata l-mustaqeem
Siraata lladheena an'amta 'alayhim ghayri l-maghdoobi 'alayhim wa laa d-daalleen
fatiha.translation:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
All praise is due to Allah, Lord of all the worlds,
the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful,
Master of the Day of Judgement.
You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help.
Guide us to the straight path,
the path of those You have blessed — not of those who earned Your anger, nor of those who went astray.
fatiha.note: The Fatiha is recited in every single unit of prayer. Say "Aameen" after it. It is the one recitation no unit can be valid without.

surah.name: A short surah
surah.phonetic:
Qul huwa Llaahu ahad
Allaahu s-samad
Lam yalid wa lam yoolad
Wa lam yakun lahu kufuwan ahad
surah.translation:
Say: He is Allah, the One.
Allah, the Eternal Refuge.
He neither begets nor is born,
and there is none comparable to Him.
surah.note: Any passage of the Qur'an you know may be recited here — Al-Ikhlas is shown because it is short and easy to memorise. Added in the first two units only.

ruku.name: Ruku — bowing
ruku.posture: Say "Allahu akbar", bow so that your back is level, hands gripping the knees, head in line with the back.
ruku.translation: Glory be to my Lord, the Most Great.
ruku.note: Said three times. Be still — do not rush out of the position.

itidal.name: Standing up from bowing
itidal.posture: Rise fully upright, arms at your sides, and stand still before going down.
itidal.phonetic:
Sami'a Llaahu liman hamidah
Rabbanaa wa laka l-hamd
itidal.translation:
Allah hears the one who praises Him.
Our Lord, all praise is Yours.
itidal.note: The first phrase is said while rising, the second once standing. Praying behind an imam, you say only the second.

sujud.name: Sujud — prostration
sujud.posture: Say "Allahu akbar" and go down. Seven parts touch the ground: forehead and nose, both palms, both knees, the toes of both feet.
sujud.translation: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.
sujud.note: Said three times. Keep the elbows off the ground and away from the sides.

jalsa.name: Sitting between the two prostrations
jalsa.posture: Say "Allahu akbar", sit up on your left foot with the right foot upright, hands resting on the thighs.
jalsa.note: Sit calmly. This short pause is part of the prayer, not a transition to rush through.

sujud2.name: Second prostration
sujud2.posture: Say "Allahu akbar" and prostrate a second time, exactly as before.
sujud2.translation: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.
sujud2.note: Said three times. This completes one unit (rak'ah). Stand up again for the next one.

tashahhud.name: Tashahhud — the testimony
tashahhud.posture: Seated as between the prostrations. Both forearms rest on the thighs: the left hand flat on the left thigh, the right hand closed and resting on the right knee, only the index finger extended. The arm is not raised — the gesture happens at knee height.
tashahhud.phonetic:
At-tahiyyaatu lillaahi wa s-salawaatu wa t-tayyibaat
As-salaamu 'alayka ayyuha n-Nabiyyu wa rahmatu Llaahi wa barakaatuh
As-salaamu 'alaynaa wa 'alaa 'ibaadi Llaahi s-saaliheen
Ash-hadu an laa ilaaha illa Llaah, wa ash-hadu anna Muhammadan 'abduhu wa rasooluh
tashahhud.translation:
All greetings, prayers and good things belong to Allah.
Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings.
Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah.
I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger.
tashahhud.note: Recited sitting after every two units. The schools transmit slightly different wordings — all are valid.

salawat.name: Blessings on the Prophet
salawat.posture: Still seated, index finger still pointing.
salawat.phonetic:
Allaahumma salli 'alaa Muhammadin wa 'alaa aali Muhammad, kamaa sallayta 'alaa Ibraaheema wa 'alaa aali Ibraaheem, innaka Hameedun Majeed
Allaahumma baarik 'alaa Muhammadin wa 'alaa aali Muhammad, kamaa baarakta 'alaa Ibraaheema wa 'alaa aali Ibraaheem, innaka Hameedun Majeed
salawat.translation:
O Allah, send Your grace upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You sent it upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim. You are indeed Praiseworthy, Glorious.
O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim. You are indeed Praiseworthy, Glorious.
salawat.note: Said in the final sitting, right after the Tashahhud. You may then make any personal supplication before the Salam.

taslim.name: Taslim — closing the prayer
taslim.posture: Turn your head to the right, then to the left.
taslim.translation: Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah.
taslim.note: Said twice — once to the right, once to the left. The prayer ends here.
